newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says no one can veto NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says no one can veto NATO expansion.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday that no outside country would be able to veto the proposed enlargement of NATO.

Speaking at a news conference, Kohl said that there had been at times "ludicrous" comments from some voices in Russia about NATO and added: "No one, and I mean no one, will have a veto over which countries can join."
"Anyone who wants to can join NATO," Kohl said, speaking at a news conference with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

Former communist states in central and eastern Europe are clamouring to slip under NATO's protective shield. Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic are leading the field to win admission, with Romania and Slovenia close behind.
The new applicants are set to be named at a special summit in Madrid in July.
Russia has been offered a special charter with NATO to run in parallel with alliance enlargement, but so far has shown no sign of dropping its virulent opposition to the plan.
